content.title: About
content.content: Stuffed mushrooms are edible fungi, usually button mushrooms or oyster mushrooms, filled with a mixture of cheese, meat, vegetables, or spices. They are often served as an appetizer or side dish and are popular in European and Asian cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mushrooms readily absorb the flavors of the stuffing, making each bite unique.
Stuffed mushrooms are commonly baked, which preserves their juiciness and aroma.
In countries such as Italy, stuffed mushrooms are a traditional holiday dish.
Mushrooms are rich in B‑vitamins and minerals like selenium and potassium.
When properly prepared, stuffed mushrooms can be kept in the fridge for up to 3 days.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Mushrooms provide niacin, riboflavin, and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Stuffed mushrooms give a feeling of fullness with relatively few calories, helpful for weight management.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant and supports immune health.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium in mushrooms helps regulate blood pressure.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Mushroom allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to mushrooms.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Stuffings often contain salt; people monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt versions.

items.title: Potential toxins
items.content: Raw or improperly cooked wild mushrooms can contain toxins; only use verified species.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Some stuffing recipes include preservatives or artificial flavorings that may not suit everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Stuffed mushrooms can be served hot as an appetizer, added to salads, pasta, or rice dishes. They reheat well in the microwave or oven until the tops are golden.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepared stuffed mushrooms in an airtight container in the refrigerator for no more than 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in bags at –18 °C; fully reheat before consumption.
